A $135.6 million derivative warrant liability sits on the balance sheet against working capital of $170.7 million. The board pairs Venkatesan with Lead Independent Director Jean-Louis Malinge (ex-CEO of silicon-photonics pioneer Kotura, sold to Mellanox 2013), Glen Riley (32-year semiconductor/optoelectronics operator, ex-Qorvo / TriQuint / Agere / Lucent), Theresa Lan Ende (Arista Networks CPO, ex-Cisco supply chain), Robert Tirva (ex-Sonim CFO/COO, IBM/Broadcom/Dropbox), and Sohail Khan (newly appointed July 2025, ex-Coherent/SiC EVP, ex-Agere CEO, ex-ViXS CEO). Chris Tsiofas retired after 13 years as Audit Committee Chair at the June 2025 AGM. chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## The Platform and Its Wager

POET Technologies entered fiscal 2025 as it had entered every prior year of its modern iteration: without commercial revenue, without a disclosed hyperscaler socket, and without a product embedded in any named volume AI cluster. What changed by December 31 was the capitalisation behind the wager. The company closed the year with [$313.4 million of cash and short-term investments](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results) — up from $53.8 million a year earlier — after a 2025 financing sequence that the [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) showed had raised $280.0 million of gross proceeds across four equity transactions. Inside the frozen window, that balance-sheet story accelerated again: POET disclosed a further $150 million January 2026 registered direct and then closed a $400.0 million registered direct with a single institutional investor on May 18, 2026. [January 2026 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-pricing-of-us-150-million-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment) Against a FY2025 net loss of $62.96 million and full-year revenue of approximately $1.07 million in non-recurring engineering fees and small product receipts, POET remained one of the purest option-value propositions in the listed photonics market.

The company is incorporated in Toronto, Ontario, with its wafer-level photonic integration line operated through POET Singapore Pte. Ltd. It carried a dual listing — NASDAQ and the Toronto Stock Exchange, both under the ticker POET — and filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on a 20-F basis as a foreign private issuer. That designation is not merely administrative: it determines disclosure cadence, governance standards, and the institutional machinery through which POET accesses capital across two markets.

## The Architecture

POET designed and licensed the POET Optical Interposer: a wafer-level photonic integration platform built around a passive substrate hosting multiple optical components — lasers, modulators, photodetectors, and filters — with minimal optical coupling loss. The platform targeted 800G and 1.6 terabit transceiver applications and positioned specifically for co-packaged optics (CPO) and external light source (ELS) modules, the two segments of the hyperscaler interconnect stack where component architecture remained most architecturally open at the snapshot date.

The interposer thesis rested on integration density and coupling efficiency. POET argued that assembling heterogeneous optical components on a single passive substrate avoided the coupling losses endemic to silicon-photonics monolithic designs while enabling the chiplet-style disaggregation that hyperscalers increasingly demanded as co-packaged optics migrated from whiteboard to rack.

## The People Calibrated for This Bet

Dr. Suresh Venkatesan has served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer since 2015. He came to POET from GlobalFoundries, where as Senior Vice President of Technology Development he led the 28nm process ramp and was instrumental in the 14nm technology transfer. Before GlobalFoundries he held multiple leadership positions at Freescale Semiconductor and was named a Freescale Fellow in 2007 for CMOS technology contributions. He holds a Ph.D. in electrical engineering from Purdue University.

Jean-Louis Malinge, Lead Independent Director since September 2017, brought the board its most directly relevant operating precedent: he ran Kotura — a silicon photonics pioneer — from 2004 until its [sale to Mellanox in 2013 for $82 million](https://www.poet-technologies.com/team/jean-louis-malinge). His presence signalled that at least one board member had lived the complete arc from platform to qualified supply chain to exit.

## Financials at the Frozen Window

| FY2025 metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Revenue (NRE + product receipts) | ~$1.07M |
| Net loss | $62.96M |
| R&D expense | $18.08M |
| SG&A expense | $25.08M |
| Approx. non-cash operating costs | ~$35M |
| Cash and short-term investments | $313.4M |
| Total assets | $328.6M |
| Derivative warrant liability | $135.6M |
| Common shares outstanding | 132.3M |
| Options + warrants outstanding | 43.2M |
| Share-count increase on full exercise | ~32.6% |

The balance sheet transformation was the defining financial event of FY2025. Total assets grew from $69.7 million at December 31, 2024 to $328.6 million at December 31, 2025, while the same [20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) recorded $280.0 million of gross proceeds from 2025 equity issuance. On the liability side, a $135.6 million derivative warrant liability represented a mark-to-market obligation tied to foreign-currency-denominated warrants rather than a current cash call. The accumulated deficit stood at approximately $297 million.

On FY2025 numbers alone, the runway was materially longer than the dossier previously suggested. The [20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) said 2025 included roughly $35 million of non-cash costs and reported $31.1 million of net cash used in operating activities, implying about a decade of runway against the year-end cash-and-investments balance before taking account of the January and May 2026 financings. By the frozen snapshot date, POET had also publicly named a far broader counterpart set than a lone Sivers relationship: FIT, Mitsubishi Electric, Lessengers, Semtech, NTT Innovative Devices, LITEON and Lumilens had all been disclosed, and Lumilens had placed an initial $50 million purchase order for EOI-based engines. [FIT](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-may-14) [Mitsubishi Electric](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-mitsubishi-electric-collaborate-to-develop-3-2t-optical-engines-for-ai-networks) [Semtech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-semtech-launch-1-6t-optical-receivers-for-ai-networks) [NTT Innovative Devices](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-partners-with-ntt-innovative-devices-on-next-gen-connectivity-solutions-to-support-ai-mobile-networking) [LITEON](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-liteon-announce-joint-development-of-optical-modules-for-ai-applications) [Lumilens](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lumilens-advance-wafer-level-photonic-integration-for-next-generation-ai-optical-networks)

## The Central Tension

The arithmetic remained stark. POET's $1.07 million of FY2025 revenue did not cover a single month of its $18.08 million R&D run rate. The company had consumed roughly $297 million of cumulative equity through the close of FY2025 without reaching commercial scale. But the capital base was no longer merely a seven-year bridge built from year-end cash: on the audited FY2025 cash-use figure it already looked closer to a decade, and the January 2026 and May 2026 financings extended that further. [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment)

The board composition added texture to the governance framing: Venkatesan's foundry-process pedigree, Malinge's Kotura-to-Mellanox arc, Theresa Lan Ende's working seat as Arista Networks' Chief Procurement Director, Glen Riley's 32 years across optoelectronics and GaAs foundry management, and Sohail Khan's Coherent silicon-carbide EVP credential collectively read as governance calibrated for precisely this transition. Whether the company could convert that enlarged balance sheet into qualified, repeatable supply-chain revenue before competing architectures closed the window remained the question the rest of this report existed to frame.

chapters.title: From planar optoelectronics to the Singapore interposer line
chapters.body:
## Origins: Gallium Arsenide and Accumulated Losses

The name encoded the thesis. POET — Planar Opto Electronic Technology — described a company that, in its earliest form, was pursuing something ambitious and speculative in roughly equal measure: the monolithic integration of electronic and optical functions on gallium-arsenide substrates. The company was incorporated in Canada and traded on Toronto-listed venture exchanges through a multi-decade arc that produced material intellectual property, a string of annual losses, and no commercial-scale product. By the time Suresh Venkatesan arrived in 2015, the accumulated deficit had grown to reflect years of platform-development expenditure without a revenue line to show for it.

What survived that era was not a product but a platform posture — the underlying conviction that photonic integration could be executed at wafer level with the economics of semiconductor manufacturing, rather than the artisanal yield economics of discrete component assembly. That conviction would be carried forward, but the substrate, the architecture, and the leadership would all change.

## The Venkatesan Pivot

The pivot Venkatesan executed upon joining in 2015 was architectural rather than incremental. He redirected the company away from the gallium-arsenide monolithic integration thesis toward the POET Optical Interposer — a wafer-level photonic integration platform built around a passive substrate that could host lasers, modulators, photodetectors, and filters, assembled with minimal optical loss. Critically, the Optical Interposer was designed to be materials-agnostic: it could accommodate III-V compound-semiconductor components alongside silicon photonic devices, which differentiated the architecture from pure silicon-photonics plays and from compound-semiconductor-only approaches. The platform thesis was that this agnosticism, combined with wafer-scale assembly economics, would produce the integration density and cost structure that hyperscale data-centre interconnect required.

The timing mattered. The broader industry was beginning to ask, seriously, whether pluggable transceiver modules — which had served data-centre optical interconnect for decades — could keep pace with the power and bandwidth demands of AI cluster architectures. Co-packaged optics, integrating optical engines directly onto switch and compute package substrates, was emerging as the architectural alternative. Venkatesan was positioning POET at precisely that transition, before the transition had a confirmed commercial schedule.

## Manufacturing in Singapore

POET's operational footprint anchored in Singapore through the establishment of POET Singapore Pte. Ltd., which operates the wafer-level photonic integration line. The geography was deliberate. Singapore offers a semiconductor manufacturing labour pool that is structurally deep — the island is home to fabrication and advanced packaging operations for several of the world's largest chip companies — and its trade relationships are not subject to the bilateral friction that complicates a China-headquartered manufacturing thesis for a company with US institutional shareholders and NASDAQ exposure. The company's 20-F geopolitical risk disclosure lists China, Singapore, and Malaysia as the Asia operations footprint, but Singapore is the manufacturing nucleus.

The choice also reflected proximity to the broader ecosystem of Taiwan-affiliated fabs and OSAT partners that populate the Singapore-Malaysia-Penang corridor. For a company in pre-qualification stage, being positioned within that cluster rather than isolated from it matters for component sourcing, process collaboration, and customer auditing logistics.

## Assembling the Board

The board build-out between 2017 and 2025 was the other pillar of the Venkatesan-era construction. Malinge (2017), Riley (2020), Lan Ende (2022), Tirva (December 2024), and Khan (July 2025) were added in sequence, each calibrated for a specific stage of the platform story. Tsiofas retired at the June 2025 AGM after 13 years as Audit Committee Chair, with Tirva as the natural successor. The full credentials of each director are detailed in the Leadership chapter.

## The 2025 Equity Sequence

In 2025, POET did not raise the year's capital in one transaction. The [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) showed four equity financings across the year that together brought in $280.0 million of gross proceeds: a $30 million May private placement, a $25 million July unit offering, a $75 million October private placement and an oversubscribed $150 million October registered direct. [May 2025 private placement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us-30-million-private-placement) [July 2025 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-completes-previously-announced-us-25m-non-brokered-public-offering) [October 2025 investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us-75-million-investment-to-accelerate-growth-in-ai-connectivity-solutions) [October 2025 registered direct](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us-150-million-oversubscribed-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) Total assets nevertheless still told the same story: they grew from $69.7 million to $328.6 million, and the financing created the warrant overhang and derivative-warrant liability detailed in the Financial Deep Dive chapter.

## Named Partnerships and the Qualification Phase

Sivers was important, but it was not the only named programme in the record by the frozen window. POET had announced a May 2024 design win with Foxconn Interconnect Technology, a September 2024 collaboration with Mitsubishi Electric on 3.2T optical engines, a March 2026 joint-development programme with LITEON, a March 2026 expansion with Lessengers into 1.6T 2xDR4 modules, a September 2025 launch with Semtech on 1.6T receiver engines, an August 2025 partnership with NTT Innovative Devices, and a May 2026 Lumilens supply-and-development agreement carrying an initial $50 million purchase order. [FIT](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-may-14) [Mitsubishi Electric](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-mitsubishi-electric-collaborate-to-develop-3-2t-optical-engines-for-ai-networks) [LITEON](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-liteon-announce-joint-development-of-optical-modules-for-ai-applications) [Lessengers](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lessengers-expand-partnership-to-deliver-1-6t-2xdr4-optical-transceivers-for-ai-network-connectivity) [Semtech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-semtech-launch-1-6t-optical-receivers-for-ai-networks) [NTT Innovative Devices](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-partners-with-ntt-innovative-devices-on-next-gen-connectivity-solutions-to-support-ai-mobile-networking) [Lumilens](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lumilens-advance-wafer-level-photonic-integration-for-next-generation-ai-optical-networks)

## What the Arc Means

A decade after Venkatesan arrived, POET's corporate arc described a company that had executed every precondition for a credible platform-bet thesis — process-discipline leadership, a materials-agnostic integration architecture, a Singapore-Malaysia manufacturing footprint with geopolitical logic, a board assembled for the specific credibility demands of the CPO transition, and a balance sheet rebuilt from $53.8 million in cash and short-term investments to $313.4 million at year-end 2025 before the additional January and May 2026 financings. [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment) What it still had not executed by the FY2025 close was material commercial revenue: approximately $1.07 million of NRE and small product receipts against a $62.96 million net loss.

The enlarged war chest purchased time, and time purchased qualification opportunities. Whether those opportunities convert — against competing architectures from Marvell, Broadcom, Intel, Ayar Labs, Lightmatter and Celestial AI, and against the continued incumbency of pluggable transceiver economics — remained the binary the next stage of the hyperscaler supply chain would answer.

chapters.title: One platform, four module applications
chapters.body:
## The platform underneath everything

The POET Optical Interposer — the wafer-level photonic integration platform described in the Snapshot — was not a product but a technology substrate. Four distinct module application areas were being developed as of the snapshot date, none at commercial volume.

## Four applications, none at volume

**800G optical transceiver modules** represented the nearest-term commercial opportunity in POET's product taxonomy as of FY2025. Built on the Optical Interposer, these modules targeted hyperscaler datacenter interconnect at the 800 gigabit-per-second line rate that had become the dominant deployment standard in large AI cluster builds through 2024 and 2025. The [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) still disclosed no customer contributing more than 10% of revenue and no volume design win, but POET's own releases showed the programme had moved beyond abstract qualification language: it announced a May 2024 design win with Foxconn Interconnect Technology for 800G and 1.6T pluggables, shipped final design samples to three unnamed technology leaders in March 2025, and received a production order worth more than $5 million from a leading systems integrator in October 2025. [FIT](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-may-14) [Q1 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results) [US$5 million production order](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-receives-5-million-production-order-for-800g-optical-engines)

POET also tried to collapse the gap between component supplier and module vendor. On March 26, 2024 it said it was entering the optical-module market with Wavelight, an 800G 2xFR4 OSFP transceiver that used POET optical-engine products internally and was due to begin customer sampling in the third quarter of 2024. That was not yet evidence of broad direct sales, but it showed management was prepared to commercialize the platform both as a component supplier and, where useful, as a reference-module vendor under its own brand. [Wavelight](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-mar-26)

The 800G lane was also where the customer roster became more specific than the earlier draft allowed. In August 2024 Luxshare Tech expanded its relationship with POET after successful testing of 800G 2xFR4 OSFP modules using POET receive engines and said selected POET engines would be integrated into existing Luxshare products already on the market. In September 2024 Mentech selected POET's transmit and receive engines for 800G development and placed initial sample orders, with POET saying module design efforts usually took six to nine months followed by another three to six months of end-customer testing. [Luxshare](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-luxshare-tech-expand-product-offerings-for-artificial-intelligence-networks) [Mentech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-selected-by-mentech-to-supply-engines-for-800g-and-1-6t-optical-modules)

**1.6T optical transceiver modules** were no longer merely conceptual by the frozen window. POET and Semtech launched 1.6T receiver optical engines for customer sampling on September 30, 2025; those engines targeted DR8 and 2xFR4 modules at 200G per lane and were said to be available immediately for qualified-customer evaluation. POET and Lessengers then announced joint development of a 1.6T 2xDR4 transceiver on March 17, 2026, with samples targeted for Q2 2026. Management described the 1.6T line as part of the company's push into next-generation AI clusters and hyperscale data-center links rather than as a distant science project. [Semtech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-semtech-launch-1-6t-optical-receivers-for-ai-networks) [Lessengers](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lessengers-expand-partnership-to-deliver-1-6t-2xdr4-optical-transceivers-for-ai-network-connectivity)

**External Light Sources for co-packaged optics** remained the third application and the most explicit CPO wedge. In September 2025, POET and Sivers announced a collaboration to combine Sivers Photonics' high-power InP DFB lasers with POET's Optical Interposer for ELS modules, with early prototypes expected in the first half of 2026 and production readiness targeted by the end of 2026. By May 2026, the light-source story had widened again: POET and LITEON announced a joint module-development programme, while the Lumilens agreement introduced the Electrical-Optical Interposer and an initial $50 million purchase order subject to successful development and qualification. [Sivers](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market) [LITEON](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-liteon-announce-joint-development-of-optical-modules-for-ai-applications) [Lumilens](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lumilens-advance-wafer-level-photonic-integration-for-next-generation-ai-optical-networks)

**Other photonic integration applications** were not blank space in the disclosures so much as a bucket of named but still early programmes. Mitsubishi Electric was working with POET on 3.2T optical engines, NTT Innovative Devices on a 100G bidirectional optical engine for mobile front-haul networks, and Quantum Computing Inc. on 400G-per-lane thin-film-lithium-niobate-modulator-based 3.2Tbps engines targeted for completion in the second half of 2026. The revenue contribution from these efforts remained small and largely non-recurring, but the counterparties themselves had been identified and the application map was wider than simple 800G pluggables. [Mitsubishi Electric](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-mitsubishi-electric-collaborate-to-develop-3-2t-optical-engines-for-ai-networks) [NTT Innovative Devices](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-partners-with-ntt-innovative-devices-on-next-gen-connectivity-solutions-to-support-ai-mobile-networking) [QCi](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-quantum-computing-inc-to-co-develop-3-2-tbps-optical-engines-for-cpo-and-next-gen-ai-connectivity)

## Revenue that tells you where the company actually is

POET recorded approximately $1.07 million in FY2025 revenue, comprising NRE fees and small product shipments: $166,760 in Q1 2025, $268,469 in Q2, $298,434 in Q3 and $341,202 in Q4. By the first quarter of 2026, the reported figure had risen to $503,389, though it remained tiny relative to the company's cost base. [Q1 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q2 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q3 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q4 2025 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q1 2026 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) NRE revenue still reflected deepening customer engagement rather than volume procurement — engineering teams paying POET to solve integration problems, not placing sustained production orders.

The March 20, 2025 sample-shipment release made the bridge between engineering revenue and hoped-for product revenue unusually explicit. POET said the transmit-engine samples were assembled at its high-volume Malaysia facility, that the receive engines had already been qualified, and that completed modules would move to end-customer qualification with production orders expected in the second half of 2025. [Sample shipments](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-ships-advanced-optical-engine-samples-to-three-global-technology-customers-for-ai-applications)

## Singapore, manufacturing, and what the filing does not say

POET's physical integration happens through POET Singapore Pte. Ltd. — the geographic logic is detailed in the Corporate History chapter. POET is a design-and-IP company, not a fab-owner: capital allocation runs through R&D ($18.08 million FY2025) and SG&A ($25.08 million), with no meaningful capex line.

What the releases did disclose, however, was more manufacturing scaffolding than the earlier chapter captured. The fourth-quarter 2024 release said POET had established a major wafer-level assembly and test facility for optical engines in Penang with Globetronics Manufacturing, equipped for an initial one million optical engines of annual capacity. The second-quarter 2025 release added NationGate Solutions in Malaysia to build light-source products and said customers had been visiting both facilities while POET qualified them for production. [Q4 2024](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2024-financial-results) [Q2 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial-results)

## The product taxonomy as investment thesis

The four applications form a portfolio of options on a single architectural bet: 800G as near-term proof point, 1.6T as retention play, ELS as CPO-specific positioning, and adjacent co-development programmes as unpriced optionality. None generated commercial volume at the snapshot date; all were funded by the $313.4 million cash position. But by the frozen window the taxonomy was no longer theoretical. It included a branded 800G module, multiple named module partners, immediate 1.6T sampling, a disclosed ELS roadmap, and a second-wave roadmap reaching out toward 3.2T.

chapters.title: The $313M war chest against the $63M operating burn
chapters.body:
## A company measured in losses, not revenues

POET's FY2025 produced a $62.96 million net loss against roughly $1.07 million of revenue — still an extraordinary ratio, but lower than the earlier draft suggested. The revenue consisted of NRE and small product deliveries: $166,760 in Q1 2025, $268,469 in Q2, $298,434 in Q3 and $341,202 in Q4. [Q1 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q2 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q3 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q4 2025 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results) The correct frame for the loss remained the same: what did POET buy with that capital, and how much time did it purchase?

## The expense walk: where the cash went

R&D expenditure for FY2025 came in at $18.08 million, of which $2.22 million was stock-based compensation. The cash component of R&D, roughly $15.86 million, funded the Singapore-based wafer-level photonic integration line and the qualification work that management was discussing across Sivers, Semtech, Lessengers and other programmes.

General and administrative expenses totalled $25.08 million. Within that figure, $3.89 million was stock-based compensation and $3.32 million was depreciation and amortisation — both non-cash. Cash SG&A was therefore closer to $17.87 million.

The earlier draft's runway math understated how much of FY2025's loss was accounting rather than cash. POET's own [Q4 2025 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results) said the year included roughly $35 million of non-cash costs, driven primarily by the fair-value adjustment to derivative warrants, while the audited [20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) reported $31.1 million of net cash used in operating activities for the full year. That operating-cash figure is the cleaner denominator for runway analysis.

The quarterly cash-flow pattern reinforced that point. Operating cash outflow was $8.7 million in Q4 2024, $8.9 million in Q1 2025, $7.7 million in Q2 2025, $2.8 million in Q3 2025, $11.6 million in Q4 2025 and $8.8 million in Q1 2026. The burn did not march upward in a straight line; it moved with program timing, working-capital movements and the increasingly real shift from prototype work to productization. [Q4 2024](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2024-financial-results) [Q2 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q3 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q1 2026](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results)

## The balance sheet expansion: four 2025 financings, then more in 2026

At December 31, 2024, POET's total assets stood at $69.7 million, with cash and short-term investments of $53.8 million. Twelve months later, total assets had grown to $328.6 million and cash and short-term investments had risen to $313.4 million. Working capital stood at $170.7 million. [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm)

The mechanism was a sequence rather than a single transaction. The 2025 capital stack comprised a $30 million May private placement, a $25 million July offering, a $75 million October investment and a $150 million October registered direct, which together produced $280.0 million of gross proceeds in the [20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm). Inside the frozen window, POET then added another $150 million January 2026 registered direct and a $400.0 million May 18, 2026 registered direct with a single institutional investor. [May 2025 private placement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us-30-million-private-placement) [July 2025 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-completes-previously-announced-us-25m-non-brokered-public-offering) [October 2025 investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us-75-million-investment-to-accelerate-growth-in-ai-connectivity-solutions) [October 2025 registered direct](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-pricing-of-us-150-million-oversubscribed-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) [January 2026 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-pricing-of-us-150-million-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment)

The underlying terms mattered because they governed the future share count as much as the cash balance:

| Financing | Securities issued | Gross proceeds | Key disclosed terms |
|---|---|---|---|
| May 22, 2025 | 6.0M common shares + 6.0M warrants | $30.0M | Single strategic investor; warrants exercisable to May 22, 2030 at C$8.32 |
| July 17, 2025 | 5.0M units | $25.0M | Each unit contained one common share and one warrant exercisable for five years at C$8.16 |
| October 7, 2025 | 13.64M common shares + 13.64M warrants | $75.0M | Single institutional investor; combined price $5.50; warrants at C$9.78 to October 2030 |
| October 28, 2025 | 20.69M common shares | $150.0M | Two new fundamental investment managers; no warrants disclosed in the release |
| January 23, 2026 | 20.69M common shares | $150.0M | Registered direct to institutional investors for corporate development and scale-up |
| May 18, 2026 | 19.05M common shares + 19.05M warrants | $400.0M | Single institutional investor; combined price $21.00; warrants at $26.25 for three years |

The balance sheet transformation was not free. Alongside the $313.4 million year-end cash balance, POET carried a $135.6 million derivative warrant liability — a non-cash fair-value line that moved with the share price — and a smaller $5.8 million convertible-debt balance.

## Runway: closer to a decade on FY2025 cash use, and longer after 2026 financings

Using the audited $31.1 million of net cash used in operating activities in 2025, the $313.4 million of year-end cash and short-term investments implied about ten years of runway even before POET raised another $150 million in January 2026 and $400 million in May 2026. [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) [January 2026 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-pricing-of-us-150-million-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment)

That mattered strategically. A potential OEM or hyperscaler evaluating the Optical Interposer no longer had reason to doubt whether POET would survive a multiyear qualification cycle. What the balance sheet bought was negotiating durability, not proof that qualification would convert.

The use-of-proceeds language in the 2025-2026 financings also showed that management was not treating the cash pile as passive treasury. The October 2025, January 2026 and May 2026 releases all pointed to targeted acquisitions, capability expansion, light-source acceleration and manufacturing scale-up rather than simple balance-sheet repair. In other words, the cash was being raised to move POET from engineering credibility toward supply-chain credibility. [October 2025 investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us-75-million-investment-to-accelerate-growth-in-ai-connectivity-solutions) [January 2026 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-pricing-of-us-150-million-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment)

This calculus still depended on burn staying roughly within the range implied by 2025 operating cash use. A sharp increase in manufacturing expansion, acquisitions or headcount could compress the runway, though the May 18, 2026 financing was explicitly raised to support that scale-up.

## Share structure and the dilution overhang

At December 31, 2025, POET had 132.3 million common shares outstanding. Against that base, the outstanding options (5.79 million) and warrants (37.36 million) implied a fully diluted share count of roughly 175.4 million shares. Stated plainly, full exercise would expand the basic year-end share count by about 32.6%. [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm)

The warrant component carried the larger structural weight. The 37.36 million outstanding warrants linked directly to the $135.6 million derivative warrant liability on the balance sheet. If those warrants were exercised as the share price appreciated, the company would gain cash but existing holders would absorb a substantial increase in the share count.

The options represented the more conventional dilution mechanism: management and employee retention instruments whose vesting schedules and strike prices were disclosed in the 20-F footnotes. By the frozen window, investors also had to account for the additional 20.69 million common shares sold in January 2026 and 19.05 million common shares plus 19.05 million warrants issued in the May 2026 registered direct. [January 2026 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-pricing-of-us-150-million-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment)

There was a second, more contingent dilution channel inside the frozen window as well. The Lumilens agreement gave Lumilens a warrant to purchase up to 22,921,408 common shares, immediately exercisable for 2,292,140 shares and then vesting in tranches as Lumilens made cumulative payments toward future purchase orders totaling up to $500 million. That instrument was not part of the December 31, 2025 capital structure, but by May 2026 it had become part of the forward dilution map. [Lumilens](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lumilens-advance-wafer-level-photonic-integration-for-next-generation-ai-optical-networks)

## The accumulated deficit: what $297 million of patience looks like

POET's accumulated deficit stood at approximately $297 million at the FY2025 close, reflecting the cumulative equity consumed since the company committed to the photonic integration platform thesis. Against that, accumulated net operating losses of approximately $180 million represented the tax-shelter asset embedded in the balance sheet — losses that could, if POET ever reached sustained profitability, shelter a meaningful portion of future taxable income.

The $297 million figure deserves to be read as historical context rather than as an indictment. Semiconductor platform companies — from InPhi to Ayar Labs to Ranovus — typically consume hundreds of millions of dollars before a component architecture reaches the volume qualification stage. POET's cumulative losses, measured against the cost basis of competing platforms developed inside better-capitalised incumbents, were not obviously outsized. What distinguished POET's position from a typical distressed pre-revenue equity was the $313 million cash cushion that, as of the snapshot date, ensured those historical losses would not be the cause of the thesis failing.

The investment question, stated plainly, was not whether POET had burned capital in the past — it unambiguously had, at scale, across more than a decade — but whether the $313 million now on the balance sheet was sufficient to survive to the moment when hyperscaler CPO adoption produced a revenue event meaningful enough to validate the accumulated investment. The financial architecture, as constructed at December 31, 2025, said the answer was probably yes. The technology and market architecture said the answer remained genuinely uncertain.

chapters.title: Four quarters of qualification engineering revenue
chapters.body:
## The baseline: three thousand dollars of revenue

When POET Technologies filed its third-quarter 2024 interim report, the revenue line disclosed $3,685 — three thousand, six hundred and eighty-five dollars — of non-recurring engineering and product receipts. For a company whose market capitalisation had been moving in multiples of tens of millions on architectural enthusiasm for co-packaged optics, it was a deliberately legible number. Not a rounding artefact, not a revenue line that could be charitably read as early commercial traction. Three thousand dollars is a figure that places the entire platform thesis in crisp relief: POET is, as a matter of public disclosure record, a pre-commercial equity at this point in its operating history.

The number mattered less as an operating fact than as a framing device for what followed.

## The quarterly progression

The arc from Q3 2024 through Q1 2026 constituted the publicly disclosed revenue history that mattered at the frozen window. The progression remained small, but it was more complete than the earlier draft suggested:

| Period | NRE & Product Revenue | Sequential Change |
|---|---|---|
| Q3 2024 | $3,685 | — |
| Q4 2024 | $29,032 | +688% |
| Q1 2025 | $166,760 | +474% |
| Q2 2025 | $268,469 | +61% |
| Q3 2025 | $298,434 | +11% |
| Q4 2025 | $341,202 | +14% |
| Q1 2026 | $503,389 | +48% |

*Sources: [Q4 2024 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2024-financial-results); [Q1 2025 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results); [Q2 2025 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial-results); [Q3 2025 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results); [Q4 2025 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results); [Q1 2026 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results)*

From $3,685 to $503,389 across six reported quarters was real movement, but it remained qualification-era movement. Full-year 2025 revenue totalled approximately $1.07 million, and the first quarter of 2026 still left the company orders of magnitude below a commercial-scale photonics revenue line.

The distinction mattered. NRE revenue is by definition non-recurring. It reflects an engineering relationship, often a time-gated evaluation, and it carries no guarantee of conversion to production. What the progression disclosed was a deepening queue of customer activity, not proof that POET had crossed into volume supply.

## Operating costs: the structural counter-narrative

While revenue moved from thousands to hundreds of thousands, expenses grew faster. The cost structure is detailed in the Financial Deep Dive chapter; the key point for the quarterly narrative is that qualification is expensive before it converts, and the company bearing that cost is POET, not the hyperscaler evaluating it.

## The financing sequence: balance-sheet transformation as the defining event

The most consequential financial event was not a revenue disclosure but the 2025-2026 financing sequence. In calendar 2025 alone, POET raised $280.0 million of gross proceeds across four equity transactions, according to the [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm). It followed that with another $150 million in January 2026 and a $400 million registered direct closed on May 18, 2026. [January 2026 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-pricing-of-us-150-million-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment) For the quarterly narrative, the key point was runway: management now had capital adequate to stay present through a long qualification cycle rather than needing near-term revenue simply to survive.

## Named programmes and the qualification engineering narrative

Sivers was important, but by the frozen window it sat inside a wider disclosed programme set. POET had named FIT, Mitsubishi Electric, Lessengers, Semtech, NTT Innovative Devices, LITEON and Lumilens, and it had announced an initial $50 million Lumilens purchase order and an earlier production order worth more than $5 million from a leading systems integrator. [FIT](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-may-14) [Mitsubishi Electric](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-mitsubishi-electric-collaborate-to-develop-3-2t-optical-engines-for-ai-networks) [Lessengers](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lessengers-expand-partnership-to-deliver-1-6t-2xdr4-optical-transceivers-for-ai-network-connectivity) [Semtech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-semtech-launch-1-6t-optical-receivers-for-ai-networks) [NTT Innovative Devices](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-partners-with-ntt-innovative-devices-on-next-gen-connectivity-solutions-to-support-ai-mobile-networking) [LITEON](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-liteon-announce-joint-development-of-optical-modules-for-ai-applications) [Lumilens](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lumilens-advance-wafer-level-photonic-integration-for-next-generation-ai-optical-networks) [US$5 million production order](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-receives-5-million-production-order-for-800g-optical-engines) The key point was still the same: these were proof-of-engagement and early commercial framework events, not yet a mature, repeatable revenue base.

## What the cadence tells a sophisticated investor

Six quarters of NRE and product revenue, read together, produced a coherent but bounded narrative. The progression from $3,685 to $503,389 represented genuine engineering progress — deeper customer engagement, a broader disclosed set of counterparties, and, by May 2026, the first sizable purchase-order framework. The balance-sheet expansion from $69.7 million of total assets at the end of 2024 to $328.6 million at the end of 2025, followed by January and May 2026 financings, materially changed the probability that POET would still be funded when hyperscaler CPO qualification decisions reached their critical phase. [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment)

What the cadence still did not produce by the frozen window was evidence of large, recognized product revenue. The company had named programmes, named collaborators and an initial purchase-order framework, but the reported income statement remained dominated by NRE and sample-stage sales. That was the honest place to leave the earnings story.

chapters.title: The GlobalFoundries CEO and his Kotura-pedigree lead independent
chapters.body:
## The Semiconductor Process Man

Venkatesan's background — Motorola SABA (2004), Freescale Fellow (2007), GlobalFoundries SVP Technology Development leading the 28nm ramp and 14nm transfer — is summarised in the Snapshot. The distinctive credential for POET is that leading a process node ramp at a tier-one foundry requires translating theoretical process physics into high-yield, high-volume manufacturing at a cadence that serves actual customers. That discipline is categorically different from managing a photonics startup's engineering team. Over his career Venkatesan accumulated more than 25 US patents and co-authored over 50 technical papers.

The logic of hiring him as Chairman and CEO becomes legible only if one accepts POET's architectural premise: that the Optical Interposer is fundamentally a wafer-level semiconductor manufacturing discipline, not an optics assembly problem. Whether that bet was correctly placed will be answered by hyperscaler qualification decisions in 2026 and 2027.

## The Kotura Precedent

Malinge is the only board member who has already done what POET is trying to do. From 2004 to 2013, he ran Kotura — a silicon photonics company deployed in three of the top five telecoms — from early-stage through its [sale to Mellanox for $82 million](https://www.poet-technologies.com/team/jean-louis-malinge). Before Kotura: 15+ years at Corning, ultimately as VP of Optical Networking Components. Since Kotura: Partner at ARCH Venture Partners (~$2B AUM) and Managing Director at YADAIS.

POET is attempting a structurally similar journey — different integration architecture, different customer segment (hyperscaler AI vs telecom), larger addressable market. Malinge's presence as Lead Independent Director signals that someone who navigated a photonics platform from development through exit finds POET's thesis credible enough to govern.

## The Working Hyperscaler Credential

Theresa Lan Ende joined POET's board as a formal director in October 2022 after the company appointed her as a board adviser on June 7, 2022 and said it would nominate her at the October 6, 2022 annual meeting. POET's own announcement described her then-current role at Arista Networks as Chief Procurement Director, following a decade as Senior Director of Global Supply Chain Management. [POET adviser announcement](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2022-jun-7)

The significance of Lan Ende's seat on the POET board was not biographical; it was structural. Arista Networks is one of the dominant vendors of high-speed Ethernet switching equipment into hyperscaler AI infrastructure builds. Lan Ende's career — spanning Arista, JDS Uniphase, Force10 Networks, Cisco Systems and ROLM Telecommunications — was supply-chain-heavy in exactly the optical and switching domains POET targeted. The Silicon Valley Business Journal named her among its Top 100 Women of Influence in 2019.

A working procurement executive at a hyperscaler-adjacent switching company occupied a seat on POET's board while the company was trying to qualify into AI-networking supply chains. The practical question — whether that background translated into a direct commercial pathway for POET — remained unanswered in public filings. What was answered was that the board had recruited exactly the customer-side operating vocabulary it previously lacked.

## Thirty-Two Years of Optoelectronics

Glen Riley joined POET's board in December 2020 and chairs its Compensation Committee. His career defies tidy summary but rewards enumeration: Asia Sales President at Lucent Technologies Microelectronics Group, based in Tokyo; Vice President at Agere Systems responsible for its high-speed and long-haul optoelectronics business; Chief Executive of Opticalis, an optical component start-up; General Manager of TriQuint Optoelectronics; General Manager of TriQuint's GaAs Foundry Business; Managing Director of TriQuint International in Singapore; and, most recently, General Manager of the Filter Solutions Business Unit at Qorvo. He graduated valedictorian from the School of Engineering at the University of Maine and completed Harvard Business School's General Management Programme in 1998.

The TriQuint years are particularly relevant to POET's technology positioning. Running a GaAs foundry business requires the same compound-semiconductor process discipline that POET's Optical Interposer architecture depends on — III-V materials, epitaxial growth, wafer-level integration — applied to a volume manufacturing context with real customers and real yield targets. Riley had three distinct subsidiary general-manager roles inside TriQuint before the company merged with RF Micro Devices to form Qorvo in 2015. Thirty-two years of compound-semiconductor and optoelectronics operating experience, distributed across multiple business unit leadership positions, is the depth of domain knowledge that a pre-revenue photonics platform company can rarely attract to its board.

## The CFO Credential and the Audit Chair Reconfiguration

Robert Tirva joined POET's board on December 5, 2024 and was appointed to the Audit Committee the same day. The [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) then recorded a second step in the transition: Tirva became Audit Committee chair on May 13, 2025, and Chris Tsiofas resigned from the board on June 27, 2025 after serving as audit-chair through that handoff. [Tirva appointment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-appointment-of-new-director) [2025 AGSM results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-provides-results-of-2025-annual-general-and-special-meeting)

The earlier draft's observation about the absence of a CFO was no longer supportable. POET's own filings and releases identified Thomas R. Mika as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer through the frozen window, including in the [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm), the [Q1 2026 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) and the [May 18, 2026 financing release](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment). Tirva's arrival therefore mattered less as a substitute for a missing finance chief than as an added public-company audit credential layered onto an already named CFO function.

## The Newest Arrival and the M&A Pattern

Sohail Khan joined POET's board on July 7, 2025, assigned to the Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee. His career carries the deepest chip-CEO M&A pattern recognition of any director on the board. At Coherent Corp. — the compound-semiconductor materials and components company formerly known as II-VI — Khan served as Executive Vice President of Wideband Gap Electronics and President of SiC, LLC, giving him operating responsibility inside one of the dominant III-V and silicon-carbide materials companies in the industry. Before Coherent, he served as CEO and Head of Strategy at Agere Systems, as President and CEO of fabless semiconductor company ViXS Systems, and as Managing Partner at K5 Innovations. His board tenures include sixteen years at LightPath Technologies, an optical-component company, and a director seat at Intersil Corporation.

The Coherent SiC credential is the most structurally adjacent operating role to POET's technology stack. Silicon carbide and the III-V compound semiconductors POET works with are both wide-bandgap or compound-semiconductor materials categories where wafer-level process discipline and materials-science depth are the moat. Running a SiC business unit inside Coherent is not the same as running a photonic interposer company, but the operational vocabulary is recognisably similar. Khan's Agere and ViXS CEO roles bring something different: pattern recognition across semiconductor company M&A cycles at multiple scale points — Agere was itself a spin-off from Lucent Technologies and was subsequently acquired by LSI Corporation in 2007.

## A Board Calibrated for One Decision

The six-director board POET carried into mid-2026 — Venkatesan, Malinge, Lan Ende, Riley, Tirva, Khan — is unusually well-credentialed for a company at its revenue stage. The composition reads as a deliberate answer to the single question the Optical Interposer thesis must answer over the next eighteen to twenty-four months: can POET get qualified in a hyperscaler CPO supply chain before competing architectures lock it out or pluggable optics continue to absorb the addressable market?

Against that question, every seat has a legible function. Venkatesan brings foundry-process discipline to the CEO chair. Malinge brings the only direct operating precedent — having done the silicon-photonics company-and-exit once already. Lan Ende brings the customer-side supply-chain credential at a hyperscaler-adjacent company. Riley brings 32 years of compound-semiconductor and optoelectronics operating depth. Tirva brings the public-company financial-execution credential the reconfigured audit function requires. Khan brings chip-CEO M&A pattern recognition and Coherent-grade compound-semiconductor operating experience.

Compare this with a board assembled for IPO execution or transformational M&A — typically heavy on investment-banking relationships, capital-markets advisors, and financial-engineering expertise. POET's board contains none of that. It is calibrated, instead, for governing a pre-revenue platform company through a technology qualification cycle that will be decided by engineering and supply-chain conversations, not by financing transactions. Whether the platform wins those conversations is the investment question. The board's composition suggests management understood what kind of governance the thesis required.

chapters.title: A pipeline of qualifications and one strategic partner
chapters.body:
## Named Counterparties, Not Yet Revenue Concentration

The core disclosure constraint in POET's FY2025 20-F was narrower than the earlier draft suggested. The filing did not show any customer contributing more than 10% of revenue, and it did not identify a hyperscaler, OEM or module maker as a reportable revenue concentration. That was different from having no named counterparties. By the frozen window, POET had publicly identified Foxconn Interconnect Technology, Luxshare Tech, Mentech, Mitsubishi Electric, Lessengers, Sivers Semiconductors, Semtech, NTT Innovative Devices, LITEON, Quantum Computing Inc. and Lumilens across module, light-source, receiver and future-roadmap programmes, while its Q1 2025 release said it had shipped final design samples to three unnamed technology leaders. [FY2025 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1437424/000149315226014253/form20-f.htm) [FIT](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-may-14) [Luxshare](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-luxshare-tech-expand-product-offerings-for-artificial-intelligence-networks) [Mentech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-selected-by-mentech-to-supply-engines-for-800g-and-1-6t-optical-modules) [Q1 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q1 2026](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results)

That distinction mattered. POET's problem was not an absence of counterparties; it was the absence of disclosed, recurring revenue concentration. The company had named relationships, design work and early orders, but the income statement had not yet caught up.

## The Qualification Topology

POET's disclosed go-to-market path ran through module makers, laser partners and optical-component collaborators rather than through named hyperscaler purchase orders. FIT selected POET optical engines for 800G and 1.6T transceiver modules in May 2024 and said those modules were intended for some of the largest end customers in the world. Mitsubishi Electric entered a 3.2T optical-engine collaboration in September 2024. Lessengers first partnered on an 800G DR8 transceiver and then expanded the relationship in March 2026 to a 1.6T 2xDR4 module, with samples targeted for Q2 2026. [FIT](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-may-14) [Mitsubishi Electric](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-mitsubishi-electric-collaborate-to-develop-3-2t-optical-engines-for-ai-networks) [Q2 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Lessengers](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lessengers-expand-partnership-to-deliver-1-6t-2xdr4-optical-transceivers-for-ai-network-connectivity)

Luxshare and Mentech filled in the middle of that route. Luxshare said in August 2024 that selected POET engines would be integrated into products already on the market after successful testing of 800G 2xFR4 OSFP modules using POET receive engines. Mentech, in September 2024, selected POET's transmit and receive optical engines for 800G pluggable-transceiver development and placed initial sample orders for engineering builds. Those were not hyperscaler purchase orders, but they were real module-maker disclosures rather than generic pipeline language. [Luxshare](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-luxshare-tech-expand-product-offerings-for-artificial-intelligence-networks) [Mentech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-selected-by-mentech-to-supply-engines-for-800g-and-1-6t-optical-modules)

POET's own Mentech release also gave the clearest primary-source clock for what qualification meant in practice. Management said optical-module design efforts usually took six to nine months, followed by an additional three to six months of end-customer testing. That timeline was company-specific rather than an industry-general estimate, and it helps explain why sample announcements mattered more than small quarterly revenue movements. [Mentech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-selected-by-mentech-to-supply-engines-for-800g-and-1-6t-optical-modules)

The light-source path was equally concrete. Sivers paired its InP DFB lasers with POET's Optical Interposer for ELS modules in September 2025. Semtech and POET launched 1.6T receiver optical engines for customer sampling on September 30, 2025. NTT Innovative Devices entered a partnership around mobile-AI connectivity on August 29, 2025. LITEON announced a joint-development programme for next-generation optical modules on March 16, 2026. Lumilens went further still: on May 14, 2026 POET said the two companies had entered a supply-and-development agreement and that Lumilens had placed an initial purchase order valued at $50 million, with revenue still contingent on successful development, qualification and manufacturing scale-up. [Sivers](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market) [Semtech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-semtech-launch-1-6t-optical-receivers-for-ai-networks) [NTT Innovative Devices](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-partners-with-ntt-innovative-devices-on-next-gen-connectivity-solutions-to-support-ai-mobile-networking) [LITEON](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-liteon-announce-joint-development-of-optical-modules-for-ai-applications) [Lumilens](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lumilens-advance-wafer-level-photonic-integration-for-next-generation-ai-optical-networks)

## Orders, Samples and What They Actually Proved

The public record before May 23, 2026 described a ladder of engagement rather than a single binary leap. Q1 2025 brought sample shipments to three major technology leaders. Q3 2025 brought two successive initial production orders from two key customers valued at more than $5.6 million, according to management. October 22, 2025 brought a separate production order worth more than $5 million from a leading systems integrator for POET Infinity optical engines. May 2026 brought the Lumilens framework, including the initial $50 million purchase order. [Q1 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2025-financial-results) [Q3 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results) [US$5 million production order](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-receives-5-million-production-order-for-800g-optical-engines) [Lumilens](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-lumilens-advance-wafer-level-photonic-integration-for-next-generation-ai-optical-networks)

The March 20, 2025 sample-shipment release explained why those orders mattered. POET said the transmit engines were being assembled at its high-volume production facility in Malaysia, that the receive engines had already been qualified, and that customers were building complete pluggable transceivers for end-customer qualification with production orders expected in the second half of 2025. In other words, the disclosure sequence moved from development samples to completed-module qualification to early production orders in the way management itself had described. [Sample shipments](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-ships-advanced-optical-engine-samples-to-three-global-technology-customers-for-ai-applications)

None of that yet meant that POET had crossed into a stable volume-revenue state. The Lumilens release itself said fulfillment and associated revenues remained subject to successful development, qualification and manufacturing scale-up. But it did mean the dossier could no longer treat POET's customer map as a blank page.

## Manufacturing Geography and Geopolitical Exposure

The earlier draft's manufacturing paragraph also understated what POET had actually disclosed. In the fourth-quarter 2024 release, the company said it had completed the acquisition of the remaining 24.8% of Super Photonics Xiamen for a total of $6.5 million payable over five years and had decided to liquidate and close the SPX operation. The same release said POET had established a wafer-level assembly and test facility for optical engines in Penang with Globetronics Manufacturing and equipped it for an initial 1 million optical engines of annual capacity. In the second-quarter 2025 release, POET added NationGate Solutions in Penang under a Master Agreement, Module Purchase Agreement and Deed of Consignment to manufacture optical engine assemblies and build light-source products. [Q4 2024](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2024-financial-results) [Q2 2025](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial-results)

By the first quarter of 2026, POET said it was headquartered in Toronto with operations in Allentown, Pennsylvania, Shenzhen, China and Singapore. By May 18, 2026, management said global headcount had risen to more than 115, the Singapore lab and office footprint had nearly tripled year over year, and Malaysia assembly space had reached 20,000 square feet. [Q1 2026](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment) The geography was therefore specific: Singapore for integration development, Penang for assembly scale-up, Shenzhen as a retained China operation, and North American commercial and engineering functions in Toronto and the US.

## The Ledger as It Stands

At the frozen window, POET's customer-and-partner map was no longer a pipeline with one disclosed anchor. It was a disclosed roster of module, laser and optical-engine counterparties, multiple sample and design programmes, one production order above $5 million, two successive production orders valued above $5.6 million in aggregate, and one conditional $50 million purchase-order framework, all still set against a revenue base that remained tiny. The right analytical conclusion was neither that POET had no commercial traction nor that it had already won hyperscale scale. It had moved into a disclosed pre-volume qualification phase with named counterparties, meaningful early orders and large unresolved execution risk.

chapters.title: Where the Optical Interposer fits in the CPO landscape
chapters.body:
## The Architectural Fork

The datacenter optical interconnect market is a dispute about where to put the light. Pluggable transceivers dominated for two decades; the AI training cluster changed the pressure: 800G and 1.6T link speeds demand that the electrical signal path between ASIC and modulator be measured in millimetres. Co-packaged optics — moving the optical engine into the switch package — hardened from theoretical to urgent. POET staked its entire thesis on this transition occurring at scale.

## How the Optical Interposer Differs from the Field

The CPO competitive landscape stratified, by 2025, into four structurally distinct approaches — and understanding POET's position requires holding all four simultaneously.

The first and dominant strand is **integrated silicon photonics**. Intel Photonics operates a silicon-only photonic integration line, internally deployed; Marvell absorbed Inphi's coherent DSP capability and has layered optical-engine assets atop it; Cisco acquired Acacia; Coherent built a vertically integrated compound-semiconductor and silicon photonics platform. These players share a common constraint: their integration approach is defined by the underlying process technology. Silicon photonics provides excellent passive components and acceptable modulators, but silicon emits no light efficiently at telecom wavelengths, requiring external or attached laser sources — a problem solved in various ways by each player, none elegantly.

The second strand is **compound-semiconductor monolithic integration** — historical InP platforms that attempt to grow lasers, modulators, and photodetectors on a single wafer of indium phosphide. High-performance, high-cost, difficult to yield at wafer scale.

The third strand is **chip-to-chip optical I/O** — Ayar Labs, Lightmatter, and Celestial AI each approached the problem from the compute-die side rather than the switch-ASIC side, designing photonic chiplets intended to replace copper die-to-die interconnect inside a package. This is a structurally different addressable market: it targets memory bandwidth and AI-accelerator die disaggregation, not the hyperscaler fabric switch.

POET's Optical Interposer falls into a fourth category: **materials-agnostic wafer-level photonic integration on a passive substrate**. The architecture is explicitly not tied to silicon as the base process. Multiple classes of active components — InP lasers, modulators, photodetectors, passive silicon filters — can be assembled onto the interposer substrate with heterogeneous integration, combining the best emitter performance from compound semiconductors with silicon's passive-optical precision. The passive substrate approach minimises optical coupling loss at each interface, which is the dominant yield-killer in heterogeneous photonic assembly. Whether POET's specific implementation of this architecture at production volumes can match the cost curve of silicon photonics incumbents remained unresolved at the snapshot date.

## The Competitive Map at a Glance

| Player | Approach | CPO Role | Revenue Scale | Key Asset |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Intel Photonics | Silicon-only integrated PIC | Optical engine supplier (internal) | Large (embedded in Intel segments) | Internal foundry, co-design with Ethernet switch |
| Marvell (Inphi) | PAM-DSP + silicon photonics optical engines | DSP and optical engine supplier | Large ($1B+ optics segment) | Inphi DSP IP, hyperscaler design wins |
| Coherent (II-VI) | Vertically integrated InP + SiPh | Transceiver, optical engine, ELS | Large ($4B+ revenue) | Vertical integration, ELS laser IP |
| Lumentum | DFB lasers, pluggable modules | Laser source supplier; pluggable incumbent | Mid ($1.5B+ revenue) | Laser yield, pluggable volume relationships |
| Broadcom (Tomahawk CPO) | Switch ASIC with integrated CPO | Switch ASIC *and* CPO platform definer | Very large ($30B+ revenue) | Tomahawk market share, hyperscaler socket |
| Ayar Labs | Intra-chip optical I/O | AI-accelerator chiplet | Pre-revenue (venture) | TSMC integration, memory-bandwidth thesis |
| Lightmatter | Photonic interconnect interposer | AI-cluster fabric (different problem) | Pre-revenue (venture) | Significant venture funding 2024–2025 |
| **POET Technologies** | **Materials-agnostic optical interposer** | **ELS module + transceiver component** | **Pre-revenue (~$1.07M NRE FY2025)** | **Heterogeneous integration IP, $313M cash** |

The table above understates the asymmetry: every named incumbent except Ayar, Lightmatter, and Celestial AI was generating hundreds of millions to billions of dollars of annual revenue at the snapshot date. POET was generating $341,000 in its strongest quarter of FY2025. The question for POET shareholders is not whether the company is better capitalised than a silicon photonics startup — the FY2025 balance sheet alone showed $313.4 million of cash and short-term investments, and the company then added a further $150 million in January 2026 and $400 million in May 2026; for a pre-revenue photonics company, the capital-availability question had been answered far more aggressively than the earlier draft allowed. [Q4 2025 results](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-fourth-quarter-2025-financial-results) [January 2026 offering](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-pricing-of-us-150-million-registered-direct-offering-of-common-shares) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment) The question is whether materials-agnostic interposer integration is structurally differentiated enough to win qualified positions in hyperscaler CPO supply chains before silicon photonics incumbents lock out non-silicon approaches at the architectural level.

## The Sivers Partnership and the ELS Use Case

The [Sivers collaboration](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-and-sivers-semiconductors-collaborate-on-external-light-sources-for-co-packaged-optics-and-next-generation-ai-market) (September 2025) is POET's most credible near-term wedge. The external light source architecture addresses a specific problem: pure CPO creates a thermal management issue at 800G and beyond because the laser is a heat source inside an already-strained thermal envelope. The ELS module places the laser array outside the switch package — still inside the rack, eliminating pluggable electrical-loss penalties — while decoupling laser cooling from ASIC cooling. POET's interposer provides the substrate; Sivers provides the InP DFB lasers. Neither company had disclosed volume design wins at the snapshot date.

## The Broadcom Demand Signal

No single commercial development in the CPO landscape carried more analytical weight in 2025 than Broadcom's Tomahawk 5 CPO programme. Broadcom — the dominant merchant silicon supplier for hyperscaler Ethernet switching — disclosed a co-packaged optical variant of the Tomahawk 5 ASIC intended for production deployment. If Tomahawk 5 CPO reaches volume deployment with major hyperscalers, it represents the clearest possible demand-side validation that the CPO architectural transition is not an engineering-conference aspiration but an operational procurement decision.

The downstream implication for POET is indirect but structural. Broadcom does not publicly disclose its optical-engine supplier list for Tomahawk CPO. But a qualified optical-engine or ELS supplier in the Tomahawk 5 CPO supply chain would have secured the most credible early-volume position in the market. POET's 20-F filing described a customer qualification pattern — engaging through hyperscaler engineering teams and OEM/ODM channels — but disclosed no Tomahawk-programme design win at the snapshot date. Nvidia's Rubin generation CPO disclosures, if they materialised, represented the second major demand-signal the market was tracking: Nvidia's internal silicon photonics roadmap and any CPO commitment at Rubin scale would multiply the addressable market for interposer-based optical engines by adding GPU-to-switch links to the already-large switch-fabric opportunity.

## Structural Position: The Platform Bet with Real Cash

Against large-cap incumbents (Coherent, Lumentum, Marvell), POET's $18.08 million R&D budget is a fraction of their spend. The thesis depends on the interposer approach being differentiated enough that hyperscaler CPO architects seek it out.

Against venture-funded competitors (Ayar Labs, Lightmatter, Celestial AI), POET's $313.4 million cash position is a structural advantage. Using FY2025 operating cash use, the year-end balance already implied roughly a decade of runway, and the January and May 2026 financings extended that further. That gave the qualification cycle — typically 18-36 months — room to run.

The honest competitive summary: POET occupies a structurally defensible niche at a moment when CPO is moving from engineering prototype to procurement conversation. The company is capitalised to survive the transition. Whether it will be qualified to benefit from it remains the open question.

chapters.title: What moved the price and what to watch
chapters.body:
## A chronology that became more commercial as the window progressed

POET's price-relevant event log between mid-2024 and May 23, 2026 was no longer just a governance story. The sequence began with product and partner disclosures — the Wavelight module launch on March 26, 2024, the FIT design win on May 14, 2024, Luxshare's expanded module partnership on August 1, 2024 and Mentech's initial sample-order disclosure on September 10, 2024 — moved through governance reshaping and a series of financings in 2025, and ended the frozen window with the Lumilens supply agreement, the first-quarter 2026 partner update and the May 18, 2026 $400 million investment. [Wavelight](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-mar-26) [FIT](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/2024-may-14) [Luxshare](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-and-luxshare-tech-expand-product-offerings-for-artificial-intelligence-networks) [Mentech](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-selected-by-mentech-to-supply-engines-for-800g-and-1-6t-optical-modules) [Q1 2026](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results) [US$400 million investment](https://www.poet-technologies.com/news/poet-technologies-announces-closing-of-us400-million-investment)

A stripped-down chronology makes the re-rating path clearer:

| Date | Event | Why it mattered |
|---|---|---|
| March 26, 2024 | Wavelight 800G module launch | First POET-branded module; moved story from platform theory toward product packaging |
| May 14, 2024 | FIT selected POET engines for 800G and 1.6T modules | First explicit design win with a major interconnect supplier |
| August 1, 2024 | Luxshare expanded partnership | Added evidence that POET engines could be embedded into existing commercial module programs |
| September 10, 2024 | Mentech selected engines and placed sample orders | Added a disclosed qualification clock at the module-maker level |
| March 20, 2025 | Samples shipped to three global technology customers | Bridged from internal product readiness to end-customer qualification |
| September 29-30, 2025 | Sivers ELS collaboration and Semtech 1.6T receiver launch | Broadened the thesis beyond 800G pluggables into ELS and 200G/lane receive paths |
| October 22, 2025 | Production order above $5 million | First clearly material single order disclosed by the company |
| November 11, 2025 | QCi 3.2Tbps collaboration | Extended the roadmap beyond 1.6T into 400G/lane design work |
| May 14-18, 2026 | Lumilens framework and $400 million financing | Joined conditional commercial scale with balance-sheet scale |

## Governance and oversight: December 2024 to July 2025
